Same three sections as sample/probes.json, same reason -- see that file's README.
works    - how a person actually asks. Expected: nearly all at rank 1.
boundary - zero shared content words. Expected NOT to return the file. Not a failure.
absent   - not in the corpus at all. Must return nothing.
The absent controls are IDENTICAL to the other probe set on purpose: holding them constant is
what makes the two corpora comparable.
The eleventh file, hello.py, has no probe. It is not markdown, so nothing indexes it and no
query can reach it. project-journal-hello-world.md is the note that makes it findable, and that

works.q: that prompt about being a senior engineer and making no mistakes
it deleted stuff I told it not to delete
a thing sitting in with the notes that no search can reach

works.note: first draft was 'why the memory system went unused for weeks' — the selftest rejected it for sharing 2 words with the FILENAME, which is a way to pass without retrieving anything

works.q: the best outcome is the confrontation that never has to happen
the joke about an assistant lighting up the ceiling

boundary.q: buttering up the model before handing it a task
boundary.why: 'buttering up' is real English for 'flattery', and a string matcher cannot see it. The natural phrasing in 'works' finds the same file at rank 1.

boundary.q: it wiped things it was told to leave alone and then signed off pleasantly
boundary.why: wiped/deleted, signed off/closing pleasantry. Shares nothing, so it returns NOTHING AT ALL -- which is the honest answer from a string matcher, not a malfunction.

boundary.q: it was built and working and still nobody reached for it
boundary.why: an entirely accurate summary of the file written in none of its words.
